Yahweh has not sent you, but you make this people trust in a lie.” (web:Jer.28.15). It closes on a personal verdict, לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.28.16, byte), matching “Therefore Yahweh says, ‘Behold, I will send you away from off the surface of the earth. This year you will die, because you have spoken rebellion against Yahweh.’” (web:Jer.28.16). The mode itself changes at verse 17, from quoted confrontation to third-person report of its fulfillment, so this row does not carry past the sentence just pronounced.

current_row.boundary_rationale: An epistolary superscription opens the unit, וְאֵ֨לֶּה֙ דִּבְרֵ֣י הַסֵּ֔פֶר אֲשֶׁ֥ר שָׁלַ֛ח יִרְמְיָ֥ה הַנָּבִ֖יא מִירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם (oshb:Jer.29.1, byte), matching “Now these are the words of the letter that Jeremiah the prophet sent from Jerusalem to the residue of the elders of the captivity, and to the priests, to the prophets, and to all the people whom Nebuchadnezzar had carried away captive from Jerusalem to Babylon,” (web:Jer.29.1) — naming the document itself a letter rather than a spoken oracle, sent from Jerusalem to the exile community by name. It continues through the courier commission, בְּיַד֙ אֶלְעָשָׂ֣ה בֶן שָׁפָ֔ן וּגְמַרְיָ֖ה בֶּן חִלְקִיָּ֑ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר שָׁלַ֜ח צִדְקִיָּ֣ה מֶֽלֶךְ יְהוּדָ֗ה אֶל נְבוּכַדְנֶאצַּ֛ר מֶ֥לֶךְ בָּבֶ֖ל בָּבֶ֥לָה לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Jer.29.3, byte), matching “by the hand of Elasah the son of Shaphan and Gemariah the son of Hilkiah, (whom Zedekiah king of Judah sent to Babylon to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon). It said:” (web:Jer.29.3), closing on the citation formula that opens the letter’s own quoted content. No koh-amar, addressee shift, or discourse imperative interrupts the superscription itself; it is pure epistolary framing naming sender, recipients, and couriers, with no oracular content of its own. Verse 4 opens the letter’s actual quoted content, addressed in Yahweh’s own voice for the first time, and this row is bounded there.
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding this superscription into the letter’s own opening instructions as one row was rejected because verses 1 through 3 carry no koh-amar or other speech formula of their own; they name the document, its sender, its recipients, and its couriers before any quoted content begins.

current_row.boundary_rationale: The letter’s own quoted content opens on the full title stack, כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֛ר יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל לְכָל הַ֨גּוֹלָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר הִגְלֵ֥יתִי מִירוּשָׁלִַ֖ם בָּבֶֽלָה (oshb:Jer.29.4, byte), matching “Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel, says to all the captives whom I have caused to be carried away captive from Jerusalem to Babylon:” (web:Jer.29.4), addressed to all the exiles by name for the first time in the letter. Settle-in instructions follow at once, בְּנ֥וּ בָתִּ֖ים וְשֵׁ֑בוּ וְנִטְע֣וּ גַנּ֔וֹת (oshb:Jer.29.5, byte), matching “Build houses and dwell in them. Plant gardens and eat their fruit.” (web:Jer.29.5). A further koh-amar recurs at verse 8, כִּי֩ כֹ֨ה אָמַ֜ר יְהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל (oshb:Jer.29.8, byte), turning from settling in to a warning against the exiles’ own prophets and diviners; this recurrence and the opening formula at verse 4 both carry the tsevaot-plus-Elohei-Yisrael stack, its own count object (sweep: 32 verses book-wide, skeleton tier), and a third koh-amar recurs at verse 10 in the distinct bare shape, כִּֽי כֹה֙ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה כִּ֠י לְפִ֞י מְלֹ֧את לְבָבֶ֛ל שִׁבְעִ֥ים שָׁנָ֖ה אֶפְקֹ֣ד (oshb:Jer.29.10, byte), matching “After seventy years are accomplished for Babylon, I will visit you and perform my good word toward you, in causing you to return to this place.” (web:Jer.29.10) — a promise of return after seventy years, carrying the minimal koh-amar-YHWH shape apart from the fuller stack, its own count object (sweep: 152 verses book-wide, skeleton tier); none of these internal recurrences carries a change of speaker or a fresh addressee of its own, so all three turns are held inside one continuous letter-address to the same audience rather than cut into separate rows. It closes on “and I will turn again your captivity, and I will gather you from all the nations, and from all the places where I have driven you,” (web:Jer.29.14); a ketiv/qere note sits in this same closing verse, on the word for captivity itself: ketiv שביתכם against qere שְׁבוּתְכֶ֗ם (oshb:Jer.29.14, WLC, single-witness). The address turns from Yahweh’s own promise to a claim quoted from the exiles’ own mouths at verse 15, marking the far edge of this row.
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Cutting fresh rows at the koh-amar recurrences opening verses 8 and 10 was considered, since each turns to a distinct topic within the letter — the false prophets, then the seventy-year promise — but rejected because none carries a frame-owner change or an addressee shift of its own; the whole eleven-verse span remains one sustained address from Yahweh to the same exile audience, held together honestly rather than split on topic alone. A closer rival stands at the 29:9/29:10 juncture, where the span closes its ninth verse verse-finally on נְאֻם יְהוָֽה (oshb:Jer.29.9, byte) immediately before כִּֽי כֹה֙ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.29.10, byte) opens the tenth; that convergence is likewise declined as a cut, since no frame-owner changes and no addressee shifts from the audience already named at oshb:Jer.29.4, so the closure corroborates continuity into the fresh koh-amar it precedes rather than a boundary.

The whole span sits inside Jeremiah’s letter, disclosed here as its embedding frame rather than argued as this row’s own operative category, which follows the restoration promise that dominates its closing verses. current_row.boundary_rationale: A claim quoted from the exiles’ own mouths opens the unit, כִּ֖י אֲמַרְתֶּ֑ם (oshb:Jer.29.15, byte), matching “Because you have said,” (web:Jer.29.15) — a setumah falls in this same opening verse. The address then turns to a party the letter has not yet named directly, כִּי כֹ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה אֶל הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ הַיּוֹשֵׁב֙ אֶל כִּסֵּ֣א דָוִ֔ד וְאֶל כָּל הָעָ֔ם הַיּוֹשֵׁ֖ב בָּעִ֣יר הַזֹּ֑את אֲחֵיכֶ֕ם אֲשֶׁ֛ר לֹֽא יָצְא֥וּ אִתְּכֶ֖ם בַּגּוֹלָֽה (oshb:Jer.29.16, byte), matching “Yahweh says concerning the king who sits on David’s throne, and concerning all the people who dwell in this city, your brothers who haven’t gone with you into captivity,” (web:Jer.29.16) — the king on David’s throne and the people who stayed in Jerusalem, rather than the exiles the letter actually addresses. A further judgment formula opens the next verse, כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת (oshb:Jer.29.17, byte) — the tsevaot-headed shape, its own count object apart from the fuller stack (sweep: 50 verses book-wide, skeleton tier) — introducing the sword-famine-pestilence sentence in the same third-person judgment. Judgment against them continues through verse 18, matching “I will pursue after them with the sword, with the famine, and with the pestilence, and will deliver them to be tossed back and forth among all the kingdoms of the earth, to be an object of horror, an astonishment, a hissing, and a reproach among all the nations where I have driven them,” (web:Jer.29.18); a ketiv/qere note sits in this same verse, on the word for horror itself: ketiv לזועה against qere לְזַעֲוָ֜ה (oshb:Jer.29.18, WLC, single-witness). It closes on the doubled closure formula, תַּ֛חַת אֲשֶֽׁר לֹא שָׁמְע֥וּ אֶל דְּבָרַ֖י נְאֻם יְהוָ֑ה אֲשֶׁר֩ שָׁלַ֨חְתִּי אֲלֵיהֶ֜ם אֶת עֲבָדַ֤י הַנְּבִאִים֙ הַשְׁכֵּ֣ם וְשָׁלֹ֔חַ וְלֹ֥א שְׁמַעְתֶּ֖ם נְאֻם יְהוָֽה (oshb:Jer.29.19, byte) — Yahweh’s own complaint, twice over, that the exiles have not heeded the prophets he kept sending (web:Jer.29.19). Whether verse 15’s quoted claim belongs with the settle-in promise that precedes it or with the Jerusalem judgment it introduces is not settled by any formula; it is read here with what follows, since the address it opens is answered only by the turn to the king and the city at verse 16. A cataphoric summons opens the very next verse, וְאַתֶּ֖ם שִׁמְע֣וּ דְבַר יְהוָ֑ה כָּל הַ֨גּוֹלָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.29.20, byte) — its own vocative addressee, belonging forward with the oracle against Ahab and Zedekiah it introduces at verse 21 rather than backward as this unit’s own closing flourish — and this row stops short of it.
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading verse 15 as the closing verse of the settle-in and restoration unit that precedes it, rather than as the opening of the Jerusalem judgment that follows, was seriously considered and is not decided here: no formula marks which side of the seam it belongs on, and the row is held at reduced confidence honestly rather than resolving that question either way. Reopening the 29:20|29:21 juncture as a cut was considered and declined: oshb:Jer.29.20 opens וְאַתֶּ֖ם שִׁמְע֣וּ דְבַר יְהוָ֑ה כָּל הַ֨גּוֹלָ֔ה (byte), the plural hear-the-word-of-YHWH summons with a vocative naming the exiles, its own count object standing in 10 verses book-wide (sweep: 10 verses, skeleton tier); the summons is cataphoric and belongs forward with the oracle it introduces rather than backward as a closing flourish, so it does not fall with what precedes. oshb:Jer.29.19 closes the judgment that precedes it on the doubled closure formula, נְאֻם יְהוָ֑ה and verse-finally וְלֹ֥א שְׁמַעְתֶּ֖ם נְאֻם יְהוָֽה (byte for each), and under the ruled ownership neum-YHWH corroborates a boundary only where a fresh onset follows — one does, at 29:20, not at 29:21. The second-person plural address the summons opens is itself sustained across the declined juncture, standing inside oshb:Jer.29.21 at הַֽנִּבְּאִ֥ים לָכֶ֛ם בִּשְׁמִ֖י שָׁ֑קֶר and verse-finally at וְהִכָּ֖ם לְעֵינֵיכֶֽם (byte for each), which argues continuity across 29:20|29:21 rather than a cut; and the koh-amar opening 29:21 carries no frame-owner change from the same divine mouth already speaking inside this letter, so it is not by itself an independent cutting onset. For these reasons the unit boundary falls at Jer.29.19|Jer.29.20, not at Jer.29.20|Jer.29.21.

current_row.boundary_rationale: A cataphoric summons back to the letter’s own audience opens the unit, וְאַתֶּ֖ם שִׁמְע֣וּ דְבַר יְהוָ֑ה כָּל הַ֨גּוֹלָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר שִׁלַּ֥חְתִּי מִירוּשָׁלִַ֖ם בָּבֶֽלָה (oshb:Jer.29.20, byte), matching “Hear therefore Yahweh’s word, all you captives whom I have sent away from Jerusalem to Babylon.” (web:Jer.29.20) — the plural hear-the-word-of-YHWH summons with a vocative naming the exiles, its own count object standing in 10 verses book-wide (sweep: 10 verses, skeleton tier), read here as belonging forward with the oracle it introduces rather than backward as the close of the Jerusalem judgment it follows. A fresh koh-amar reopens inside this same letter, כֹּֽה אָמַר֩ יְהוָ֨ה צְבָא֜וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל אֶל אַחְאָ֤ב בֶּן קֽוֹלָיָה֙ וְאֶל צִדְקִיָּ֣הוּ בֶן מַֽעֲשֵׂיָ֔ה הַֽנִּבְּאִ֥ים לָכֶ֛ם בִּשְׁמִ֖י שָׁ֑קֶר (oshb:Jer.29.21, byte), matching “Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel, says concerning Ahab the son of Kolaiah, and concerning Zedekiah the son of Maaseiah, who prophesy a lie to you in my name:” (web:Jer.29.21) — the full title stack carried in Yahweh’s own mouth within the letter Jeremiah has sent to the exiles, now naming two further parties directly for the first time, Ahab and Zedekiah, prophesying falsely in Yahweh’s name among the exiles themselves. Their sentence names the king who will kill them, בְּיַד֙ נְבֽוּכַדְרֶאצַּ֣ר (oshb:Jer.29.21, byte) — a resh-family spelling of Nebuchadnezzar’s name, distinct from the nun-family forms spelled earlier in this same letter at oshb:Jer.29.1 and oshb:Jer.29.3. The unit continues through the curse formula built on both their names — Ahab’s own name shifting spelling between the two verses, the fuller אַחְאָ֤ב at oshb:Jer.29.21 (byte) against the shorter, kaf-prefixed וּכְאֶחָ֔ב at oshb:Jer.29.22 (byte), each its own count object standing at one verse book-wide (sweep: skeleton tier, finals-normalized), disclosed here rather than silently harmonized — and closes on the rationale for the sentence, יַ֡עַן אֲשֶׁר֩ עָשׂ֨וּ נְבָלָ֜ה בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל וַיְנַֽאֲפוּ֙ אֶת נְשֵׁ֣י רֵֽעֵיהֶ֔ם וַיְדַבְּר֨וּ דָבָ֤ר בִּשְׁמִי֙ שֶׁ֔קֶר אֲשֶׁ֖ר ל֣וֹא צִוִּיתִ֑ם וְאָנֹכִ֛י (oshb:Jer.29.23, byte), matching “because they have done foolish things in Israel, and have committed adultery with their neighbors’ wives, and have spoken words in my name falsely, which I didn’t command them. I am he who knows, and am witness,” (web:Jer.29.23); a ketiv/qere note sits in this same closing verse: ketiv הו ידע against qere הַיּוֹדֵ֥עַ (oshb:Jer.29.23, WLC, single-witness), alongside a separate OSHB exegesis note at the same verse (single-witness apparatus, not text bytes). The address turns to a third, differently-named figure at verse 24, Shemaiah the Nehelamite, which is where this row ends.
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Reopening the 29:20|29:21 juncture as a cut was considered and declined: oshb:Jer.29.20 opens וְאַתֶּ֖ם שִׁמְע֣וּ דְבַר יְהוָ֑ה כָּל הַ֨גּוֹלָ֔ה (byte), the plural hear-the-word-of-YHWH summons with a vocative naming the exiles, its own count object standing in 10 verses book-wide (sweep: 10 verses, skeleton tier); the summons is cataphoric and belongs forward with the oracle it introduces rather than backward as a closing flourish, so it does not fall with what precedes. oshb:Jer.29.19 closes the judgment that precedes it on the doubled closure formula, נְאֻם יְהוָ֑ה and verse-finally וְלֹ֥א שְׁמַעְתֶּ֖ם נְאֻם יְהוָֽה (byte for each), and under the ruled ownership neum-YHWH corroborates a boundary only where a fresh onset follows — one does, at 29:20, not at 29:21. The second-person plural address the summons opens is itself sustained across the declined juncture, standing inside oshb:Jer.29.21 at הַֽנִּבְּאִ֥ים לָכֶ֛ם בִּשְׁמִ֖י שָׁ֑קֶר and verse-finally at וְהִכָּ֖ם לְעֵינֵיכֶֽם (byte for each), which argues continuity across 29:20|29:21 rather than a cut; and the koh-amar opening 29:21 carries no frame-owner change from the same divine mouth already speaking inside this letter, so it is not by itself an independent cutting onset. For these reasons the unit boundary falls at Jer.29.19|Jer.29.20, not at Jer.29.20|Jer.29.21. Splitting the curse-formula of verse 22 from the naming and sentence of verse 21 into its own row was rejected because it is grammatically bound back to Ahab and Zedekiah by name, one continuous judgment rather than a fresh address.

current_row.boundary_rationale: A third named figure opens the unit, וְאֶל שְׁמַעְיָ֥הוּ הַנֶּחֱלָמִ֖י תֹּאמַ֥ר לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Jer.29.24, byte), matching “Concerning Shemaiah the Nehelamite you shall speak, saying,” (web:Jer.29.24) — the unit’s own front seam opens on the conjunctive וְאֶל, a byte-true continuity signal disclosed here rather than passed over; it does not argue against the cut because it is the ordinary narrative connective introducing Jeremiah’s next commissioned reply rather than a continuation of the address just closed — the addressee shifts at once to Shemaiah the Nehelamite, commissioned as the subject of Jeremiah’s own reply rather than addressed directly, the tier-1 signal the seam actually rests on. Yahweh’s own governing formula opens this stretch of the reply, כֹּֽה אָמַ֞ר יְהוָ֧ה צְבָא֛וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל (oshb:Jer.29.25, byte), a koh-amar-headed member of the full title-stack object (sweep: 31 verses book-wide, skeleton tier), governing the charge that אַתָּה֩ שָׁלַ֨חְתָּ בְשִׁמְכָ֜ה סְפָרִ֗ים (oshb:Jer.29.25, byte) — letters, plural, the medium the bytes actually carry here, distinct from the single letter Zephaniah reads back at the report’s own close. The reply quotes Shemaiah’s own hostile letter back at him, including its rebuke naming Jeremiah by his home village, וְעַתָּ֗ה לָ֚מָּה לֹ֣א גָעַ֔רְתָּ בְּיִרְמְיָ֖הוּ הָֽעֲנְּתֹתִ֑י הַמִּתְנַבֵּ֖א לָכֶֽם (oshb:Jer.29.27, byte), matching “Now therefore, why have you not rebuked Jeremiah of Anathoth, who makes himself a prophet to you,” (web:Jer.29.27) — a defective spelling of the gentilic naming that village. It closes on a narrative report explaining how this exchange became known, וַיִּקְרָ֛א צְפַנְיָ֥ה הַכֹּהֵ֖ן אֶת הַסֵּ֣פֶר הַזֶּ֑ה בְּאָזְנֵ֖י יִרְמְיָ֥הוּ הַנָּבִֽיא (oshb:Jer.29.29, byte), matching “Zephaniah the priest read this letter in the hearing of Jeremiah the prophet.” (web:Jer.29.29). A fresh word-event formula opens at verse 30, turning from this narrative report to Yahweh’s own word to Jeremiah, and the row does not extend past that opening.
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Closing this row at verse 28, immediately after the quoted content of Shemaiah’s own letter, and reading verse 29 as the opening of the row that follows, was rejected because verse 29’s report refers back to this letter by name and completes the account of how it was heard, rather than introducing the fresh word-event formula that actually opens the next unit at verse 30.

A commissioned sentence follows, opening לָכֵ֞ן כֹּֽה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Jer.29.32, byte), matching “therefore Yahweh says,” (web:Jer.29.32), naming its subject at once, הִנְנִ֨י פֹקֵ֜ד עַל שְׁמַעְיָ֣ה הַנֶּחֱלָמִי֮ וְעַל זַרְעוֹ֒ לֹא יִהְיֶ֨ה ל֜וֹ אִ֣ישׁ יוֹשֵׁ֣ב בְּתוֹךְ הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֗ה וְלֹֽא יִרְאֶ֥ה בַטּ֛וֹב אֲשֶׁר אֲנִ֥י עֹשֶֽׂה לְעַמִּ֖י (oshb:Jer.29.32, byte), matching “Behold, I will punish Shemaiah the Nehelamite and his offspring. He will not have a man to dwell among this people. He won’t see the good that I will do to my people,” (web:Jer.29.32) — Shemaiah the Nehelamite, closing both the letter and this range on his personal verdict. A setumah and a doubled paseq both fall in this closing verse.

current_row.boundary_rationale: A prose-sermon superscription opens the unit, הַדָּבָר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָיָ֣ה אֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֔הוּ מֵאֵ֥ת יְהוָ֖ה לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Jer.30.1, byte), matching “The word that came to Jeremiah from Yahweh, saying,” (web:Jer.30.1) — the hadavar-asher-hayah shape that opens the consolation core's own parent frame. A command to write follows without any change of speaker, כֹּֽה אָמַ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לֵאמֹ֑ר כְּתָב לְךָ֗ אֵ֧ת כָּל הַדְּבָרִ֛ים אֲשֶׁר דִּבַּ֥רְתִּי אֵלֶ֖יךָ אֶל סֵֽפֶר (oshb:Jer.30.2, byte), matching “Yahweh, the God of Israel, says, ‘Write all the words that I have spoken to you in a book.” (web:Jer.30.2) — write every word spoken into a book. The content commanded to be written follows at once, closing on the promise itself: כִּ֠י הִנֵּ֨ה יָמִ֤ים בָּאִים֙ נְאֻם יְהוָ֔ה וְ֠שַׁבְתִּי אֶת שְׁב֨וּת עַמִּ֧י יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל וִֽיהוּדָ֖ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה וַהֲשִׁבֹתִ֗ים אֶל הָאָ֛רֶץ אֲשֶׁר נָתַ֥תִּי לַאֲבוֹתָ֖ם וִֽירֵשֽׁוּהָ (oshb:Jer.30.3, byte), matching “For, behold, the days come,’ says Yahweh, ‘that I will reverse the captivity of my people Israel and Judah,’ says Yahweh. ‘I will cause them to return to the land that I gave to their fathers, and they will possess it.’” (web:Jer.30.3). A third-person rubric then names what has just been given, וְאֵ֣לֶּה הַדְּבָרִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֨ר דִּבֶּ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה אֶל יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל וְאֶל יְהוּדָֽה (oshb:Jer.30.4, byte), matching “These are the words that Yahweh spoke concerning Israel and concerning Judah.” (web:Jer.30.4) — dropping out of quoted divine speech into the narrator's own summary of it. The imperative that follows at verse 2, כְּתָב לְךָ֗ אֵ֧ת כָּל הַדְּבָרִ֛ים אֲשֶׁר דִּבַּ֥רְתִּי אֵלֶ֖יךָ אֶל סֵֽפֶר (oshb:Jer.30.2, byte), is a commissioning write-command addressed to the same figure the header already names, הַדָּבָר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָיָ֣ה אֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֔הוּ (oshb:Jer.30.1, byte), so the address is specified rather than reopened; the messenger formula standing at the same verse involves no frame-owner change: the mouth stays the same across these verses, so neither form reaches the internal-seam classes that cut, and the whole four-verse frame stands as one unit. A fresh koh-amar opens the first poem at verse 5, matching “For Yahweh says: ” (web:Jer.30.5), and this row stops short of that onset.
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Cutting a fresh row at verse 4's shift from quoted divine speech into third-person rubric was considered, since the mode plainly changes there; it is rejected because no addressee shift, koh-amar onset, or discourse imperative marks that specific turn, and the rubric functions as this same frame's own closing heading rather than an independent unit.
